article.name: Chitta Field
article.summary: Chitta Field is a local Rust memory library and C FFI with an append-only log, snapshots, and in-memory retrieval indexes. This pinned source review records implementation structure and documented limitations, not runtime or benchmark results.

who_what.text: The README describes Chitta Field as a Rust backing-store library for the cc-soul daemon with a C FFI. This review covers the library source and documentation, not a live service or deployed authorization layer.

architecture.text: The README presents an append-only operation log, in-memory retrieval indexes, and periodic binary snapshots. The payload and mutable state are separate records: payloads hold content, realm, embedding and source fields, while state holds deletion, strength, confidence, decay and lifecycle fields.

The log source defines per-writer segment formats, CRC-protected records, a SHA-256 previous-record chain, and a vector-space stamp in V3 headers. Snapshot code stores versioned state and sidecars; these persistence mechanisms were inspected but not exercised.

behavior.text: put_memory validates embedding dimensions, computes a content identity hash, checks exact duplicates and may reinforce a near-duplicate within the same realm when embeddings are available. New payloads are logged before in-memory insertion. source_session and source_tool are optional recorded fields.
The inspected update_state method logs and applies state deltas for confidence, strength, decay, pinning, and access. This review did not trace all content-replacement operations end to end.

forget is a soft delete: it synchronizes a delete operation, marks state deleted, removes active index entries, and invalidates sourced triplets. The source path does not show physical erasure from every prior WAL segment, snapshot, replica, or backup.

Semantic recall queries the ANN index with an optional realm filter and scores hits using memory state. Separate keyword, temporal, HDC, and other retrieval lanes exist; the C FFI also exposes a hybrid fallback endpoint. No retrieval quality was measured.

scope.text: Memory payloads carry a realm and retrieval APIs can filter by it; an absent realm is unscoped. The inspected library calls do not establish authenticated tenant isolation or authorization enforcement, and no cross-scope probes were run.

provenance.text: Payloads can retain source session and tool, and the payload type includes a provenance field. In the inspected PutPayloadOp conversion, provenance is initialized to the literal human, independently of source_session/source_tool. Ordinary recall claim-level citation behavior and provenance completeness across all write paths remain unknown.

efficiency.text: The source includes bounded candidate retrieval and multiple index structures; the README describes sub-millisecond cortical recall and HNSW/LSH/product-quantized retrieval. These remain documentation and implementation claims, not measurements in this review.
WAL recovery emits diagnostic logs, and the locking notes describe lock contention and slow filesystem calls. No system execution, test, benchmark, profile, or telemetry session was run.

metrics.source_evidence: Multiple recall APIs and score fields exist.
State/status and update operations exist; end-to-end correction quality was not checked.
Soft-delete path marks state and removes active indexes.
Optional realm filters are visible in retrieval APIs.
Session/tool lineage fields exist; claim-level citation behavior was not established.
README describes performance goals; no timing samples were collected.
No token or provider-cost observations were collected.
WAL, snapshots, and sidecars exist; no bytes-per-memory measurement was collected.

limits: No system commands, tests, benchmarks, or runtime workloads were run.

The review cannot establish retrieval accuracy, abstention calibration, correction behavior, deletion completeness, cross-tenant security, crash recovery correctness, multi-writer convergence, provider behavior, latency, token/cost usage, or storage efficiency.
THEORY.md documents non-commutative updates and snapshot manifest conflict risks in the multi-writer model; README-level NFS-safety claims are not runtime guarantees established by this review.

benchmark.note: No Chitta Field system command, test, or workload was executed. Project metrics, fixture, and initial execution-status record are protocol references and contain no measured Chitta Field result.
